summary.headline: UltraTech Q4 FY26: consolidated EBITDA/ton of INR1,253 (ex-West Asia ~INR1,240), 200 MTPA capacity crossed, dividend INR240/share proposed.
summary.overview: UltraTech crossed 200 million tonnes of Indian cement capacity a year ahead of target and completed 100% brand migration for India Cements and Kesoram at end-March 2026. Q4 consolidated volumes were above 44 million tonnes (brand volume up 19% YoY), grey cement prices rose about 2.5% across most geographies, and consolidated EBITDA per tonne was INR1,253 versus INR1,225 in Q4 FY25 (ex-acquired assets INR1,296). West Asia conflict is a headwind on fuel, packing bags (about INR90 crore extra bag cost in March), freight and forex mark-to-market (about INR120-130 crore). Management guided 7-8% sustainable volume growth, double-digit volume growth for FY27, and a Board-proposed dividend of INR240 per share for FY26.

segments.name: India Cements (acquired)
segments.commentary: Q4 EBITDA INR497/t vs INR333/t in Q2 and INR305/t in Q3; 2.73 Mt of 3.12 Mt Q4 volume was on UltraTech brand. Management says true economics are about INR670/t after tolling margin booked in UltraTech books, and targets over INR1,000/t by FY28.

segments.name: Kesoram (acquired)
segments.commentary: Already operating at over INR1,000/t EBITDA in Jan-Mar 2026 quarter, in line with southern peers, per CFO.

segments.name: UAE operations
segments.commentary: About 5 Mt capacity; EBITDA INR278 crore in Q4 vs INR267 crore in Q3; utilisation recovered from about 80% after drop during the war; all bulk, no bag cost.

segments.name: Cable and wire business
segments.commentary: About INR800 crore of INR1,800 crore capex spent; management indicated launch could come in the first month of Q3 FY27 versus earlier commitment of Q3.

guidance_outlook: Sustainable volume growth of 7-8% per annum; management targets double-digit volume growth for FY27. Industry growth estimated at 6-7% for Q4 and about 6.5% for FY27.
Capacity: 200 Mtpa crossed; committed further 37 Mt taking capacity above 242.5 Mtpa in phases by FY28; plans beyond 240 Mtpa being developed.
Capex of about INR8,000-10,000 crore every year for the foreseeable future, funded from balance sheet; leverage to stay below 1x net debt/EBITDA after growth capex.
Efficiency programme: INR185/t achieved on nominal basis; target of over INR300/t now expected to be exceeded by FY28.
Clinker factor (cement-to-clinker ratio) target of about 1.54x by FY28, from 1.48x; 85% green power target by FY30 (43% today).
capex_capacity: Capacity 200 Mtpa in India (about 196 Mt India capacity mentioned); the acquired India Cements and Kesoram assets make up about 13% of consolidated capacity.
India Cements: INR1,592 crore committed for efficiency improvement plus INR400 crore for capacity expansion; Kesoram: INR400-500 crore cost-improvement capex.
Green energy: 1.8 GW platform; 43% of power from green sources; no thermal capacity to be added, per management, with more WHRS and renewable tie-ups.
Lead distance reduced to 367 km; bulk terminal network expanding including new Lucknow facility.
Capacity utilisation: about 90% across network in Q4 with average above 80%.
demand_pricing: Grey cement prices up about 2.5% in most geographies in Q4 on improved trade mix and premiumisation; cement price hike taken in April 2026 and management expects it to stay.
Trade mix about 65-67%, not diluted; infrastructure share was weaker in Q4 due to end of high-speed rail work in Gujarat.
Bag costs rose from INR9 to about INR15 per bag in March, now about INR13-14; management says price increases already offset about INR6/bag increase.
Fuel: average fuel cost about INR1.77/kcal, may rise to about INR1.8 in June quarter; long-term fuel contracts seen as favourable going forward.
Management sees no supply shortage of bags or pet coke; dispatches unaffected. Demand seen steady; slowdown noted in last 15 days of March around West Bengal and Tamil Nadu elections.
Management attributed cement's relatively muted price hikes versus steel, PVC and agri inputs to industry fragmentation.

qa_highlights.question: Will payout ratio stay high given internal accrual funding of capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is possible if the company and cement market perform well; the Board decides. Capex plan is INR8,000-10,000 crore a year funded from balance sheet with rising operating cash flows.

qa_highlights.question: How much of realisation gain is from brand transition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said brand transition helped significantly since only 0.39 Mt of India Cements' 3.12 Mt Q4 volume was non-UltraTech brand; other operational levers also contributed.

qa_highlights.question: Cost impact of West Asia conflict and June-quarter outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental bag cost of about INR90 crore in March, not to be annualised; fuel expected only slightly higher in June quarter; forex mark-to-market about INR120-130 crore charged within EBITDA; diesel impact not yet factored in.

qa_highlights.question: How much more can India Cements EBITDA rise and what share is from cost versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR200/t of India Cements EBITDA sits in UltraTech books; INR800/t in India Cements books; further efficiency of about INR200/t still to come, with price increases and operating leverage taking it beyond INR1,000/t.

qa_highlights.question: Why has cement lagged other building materials in price hikes, and can costs be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to industry fragmentation; said price increases typically come in Q1 of the fiscal and that prices will be raised as costs rise.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for merging India Cements and status of legal cases, and RCB ring-fencing?
qa_highlights.answer: Legal cases inherited are old with no movement; merger to follow once risks are resolved. Management said UltraTech's balance sheet has been ring-fenced and no funds have moved for other purposes.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: fuel (pet coke at about USD160/t in the questions), diesel costs not yet factored in, and July-September ripple effects on fuel and bags.
Forex: USD 950 million borrowings fully hedged but marked to market at INR94.85/USD; a sharp rupee move can hit EBITDA (about INR30/t per management).
Whether cement price hikes taken in April 2026 stick given industry-wide cost pressure and monsoon seasonality.
Pace of India Cements EBITDA gains toward INR1,000/t and pending legal cases before further integration/merger of India Cements.
Cable and wire business launch timing (targeted early Q3 FY27) and dividend sustainability beyond FY26.
summary.management_tone: Confident and celebratory on FY26 delivery and capacity milestones, but guarded on near-term West Asia cost outlook, repeatedly saying it is too early to quantify diesel and fuel impacts. Evasive on specific dividend payout targets and on India Cements merger timing.
key_quotes: UltraTech crossed 200 million tons of cement production capacity in India, a first for any company in a single country outside of China.
We said we would do these things, we have done them and we enter fiscal '27 in a stronger strategic position than at any point in our history.
We are not keeping cash on balance sheet out of uncertainty. We are sharing it because we can and because we have planned carefully enough to do so without any constraint.
Not a penny has moved from UltraTech balance sheet for any other purposes.

growth.why: Management guides 7-8% sustainable volume growth and double-digit volume growth for FY27, backed by 200 Mtpa crossed, 37 Mt further capacity by FY28 (to 242.5+ Mtpa), 90% utilisation, and INR8,000-10,000 crore annual capex; the timing of much of the volume push is not tied to specific commissioning dates.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: India Cements EBITDA rose from INR305/t in Q3 to INR497/t in Q4 (about INR670/t true economics), efficiency programme at INR185/t vs target over INR300/t now exceeded by FY28, and April 2026 price hike expected to stick; offset by West Asia fuel and bag costs (about INR90 crore extra bag cost in March) and INR120-130 crore forex MTM.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 37 Mt committed to take capacity above 242.5 Mtpa in phases by FY28 and under construction, with 200 Mtpa crossed already, but no specific commissioning quarter is given for most of it.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets double-digit volume growth for FY27 and 7-8% sustainable, against industry growth of about 6.5% for FY27, with Q4 consolidated volume above 44 Mt and brand volume up 19% YoY, though timing of the push is not tied to commissioning dates.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex of INR8,000-10,000 crore a year is already stated as a firm plan, and utilisation is about 90% across the network (average above 80%), so further capacity announcements (plans beyond 240 Mtpa being developed) are likely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Efficiency target of over INR300/t is now expected to be exceeded by FY28 and price hikes taken in April 2026 are expected to stick, but West Asia diesel and fuel impacts are not yet factored in.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Fuel may rise to about INR1.8/kcal in the June quarter, diesel impact is not yet factored, July-September ripple effects on fuel and bags are flagged, and a sharp rupee move hits about INR30/t on USD 950 million borrowings.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Q1 FY27 (first month of Q3 FY27 per call wording)
rows.why: Cable and wire business has about INR800 crore of INR1,800 crore capex spent, with launch guided for the first month of Q3 FY27 versus an earlier Q3 commitment.

rows.label: April 2026 cement price hike sticks
rows.why: Grey cement prices rose about 2.5% in Q4 and the April hike is expected to hold, but management flags industry cost pressure and monsoon seasonality as risks.

rows.label: India Cements EBITDA to above INR1,000/t by FY28
rows.why: India Cements EBITDA is INR497/t in Q4 (INR670/t with tolling margin) from INR333/t in Q2, with about INR200/t of further efficiency still to come, and management has committed to this target.

rows.label: India Cements merger
rows.why: Merger to follow only once inherited legal cases are resolved, and management gave no timeline and was evasive on it.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 200 Mtpa milestone, brand migration, capex plan and FY27 double-digit volume target, but guarded on West Asia fuel and diesel costs, dividend payout and India Cements merger timing; analysts pushed on India Cements margin gap, pricing pass-through and cost pressure.
